notes: Partial (conjecture ladder 2026-11-08): (R2) no even n with exactly three distinct prime factors satisfies 3c(n) = n + 2, for every p (Lean three_c_ne_two_and_two_odd, two_mixed); (R4/R5) for each K finitely many solutions with all primes 2 mod 3 and omega <= K, and for each K and each prime p = 1 mod 6 finitely many n = pB with omega(B) <= K (Dickson-type compactness, every limit equation fails mod 3); (R6) exceptional solutions up to x number O(x^(1/2)); (R8) no exceptional solution with three prime factors and p <= 10^5 (complete search with proved bounds). Boundary: three prime factors uniformly in p; posed Conjecture L2 (p x^2 y^2 + 2 = (p+2)(x^2-x+1)(y^2-y+1) only at (2, 8, 4)). Outside Lean: R4-R8 on paper and by computation (k3solve.py), and the closed forms and multiplicativity of c that R2 takes as hypotheses.

notes: Partial (conjecture ladder 2026-11-08). Lean pass 2026-11-08: the hypotheses of R2 are proved for cubeCount n = #{x^3 mod n : 0 <= x < n} (A046530): multiplicativity (cubeCount_mul, CRT) and the closed forms at prime powers (cubeCount_prime_pow_two, cubeCount_prime_pow_one, via c(p^f) = #unit cubes + c(p^(f-3)) and the unit-group order). R2 (no even n with exactly three distinct prime factors satisfies 3c(n) = n + 2) is now three_cubeCount_ne_two_and_two_odd with no hypotheses; A123365_mathlib.lean likewise gives three_cubeCount_ne_of_two_factors and three_cubeCount_eq_one_factor unconditionally. Still on paper: R4/R5 (finiteness for bounded omega), R6 (O(x^(1/2))), R7, and R8 (reduction plus complete search k3solve.py for omega = 3, p <= 10^5). Outside Lean: R4-R8 (paper and computation); R2 and the one- and two-prime-factor theorems need only reading cubeCount as A046530.
